headline: High: Goose’s broad shell/filesystem/MCP defaults can overwrite or exfiltrate Cognee-managed support data; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP and reads/writes the filesystem, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could be treated as instructions. Cognee stores documents, workflows, and support history, creating a plausible injection source. Cognee’s self-isolation helps, but Goose’s permissive tool surface keeps the pathway open.
conditions: IF Goose ingests Cognee-produced files or MCP output as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents share a writable workspace or exchanged files
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents
Separate Cognee outputs into a read-only directory
Add provenance tags to all shared artifacts
Require manual approval before Goose acts on Cognee text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Goose has broad network egress plus filesystem read/write and can use MCP. If Goose receives Cognee-managed files or session memory, it can transmit sensitive content to external model providers or MCP servers. Cognee’s allowlisted egress does not neutralize Goose’s broader outbound paths.
conditions: IF Cognee data is placed in a directory Goose can read
IF Goose is configured with external model providers or remote MCP servers
mitigations: Restrict Goose to a redacted workspace
Remove sensitive files from shared directories
Use local-only providers for Goose
Audit MCP endpoints before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Goose egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write or mutate shared state: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and Goose explicitly writes the filesystem and modifies git state. Goose also shares state via filesystem across instances. Without locking, concurrent edits can corrupt files or git history in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working tree
IF Goose and Cognee write overlapping files or git refs without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and git state, so if it consumes Cognee outputs as authoritative, a mistaken Cognee decision can cascade into code changes or commits. Cognee’s outputs include decisions and workflows, which Goose may operationalize without verification unless explicitly gated.
conditions: IF Goose uses Cognee outputs as direct task instructions
IF Goose is allowed to commit or execute shell actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Add a verification step before Goose acts
Limit Goose to draft-only mode
Keep Cognee outputs advisory, not authoritative
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Goose handles files in the user filesystem and can egress broadly. If EU or regulated customer data is routed through Goose, residency or retention obligations can be breached. Cognee’s docs-only status does not provide a compensating compliance control.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is stored in Goose-readable files
IF Goose sends those files to non-approved external services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose workspaces
Use region-approved providers only
Shorten retention on shared artifacts
Review logging settings before use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
